feeSubtotal.scope: Sum of 14 non-overlapping mapped fee streams (fee policy of run 20261012T055809Z); 5 overlapping venues are shown individually and never added.

creatorEarnings.scope: DefiLlama supply-side revenue: fees paid to coin creators and, per venue definition, holders, referrers or traders. Same venues in both weeks; venues without a definition are excluded, not zero.

venues.name: pump.fun
venues.creatorEarningsDefinition: Creator fees paid out to coin creators and cashback returned to traders/holders of the coin.

venues.name: StonkFun
venues.excludedReason: Contains LaunchLab platform fees; post-migration component not separated
venues.creatorEarningsDefinition: Creator and flywheel shares of fees, measured when they are paid out.

venues.name: Pons
venues.creatorEarningsDefinition: Includes swap fees to creators, taxes (optional) to creators and buybacks (if enabled by creators) of meme tokens

venues.name: Flap.sh
venues.creatorEarningsDefinition: Token tax routed outside the protocol Safe: V1 TaxSplitter beneficiary payouts, plus V2/V3 TaxProcessor market and dividend buckets.

venues.name: LaunchLab
venues.creatorEarningsDefinition: Fees paid out to the launch platform (e.g. StonkFun, LetsBonk) and to the token creator.

venues.name: BONK.fun
venues.excludedReason: Shares LaunchLab curve fees; post-migration component not separated

venues.name: Genius.fun
venues.creatorEarningsDefinition: Creator-selected destination allocations (Foundation or creator), creator shares and accrued funding for buybacks of individual launched meme tokens, calculated from immutable per-launch policies with contract integer rounding.

venues.name: Argus World
venues.creatorEarningsDefinition: The rest of the fees, which leave the protocol divided at the weights each launch fixed at creation: the token creator's share, the dividends paid to holders of that launched token, the share added back into the launch's permanently locked liquidity, the share used to buy and burn the launched token, and on Portal 8 the share used to buy the launched token and lock it permanently.

venues.name: Meteora DBC
venues.creatorEarningsDefinition: The portion of the trading fees paid to LPs and referrals.

venues.name: Binance Alpha
venues.excludedReason: Execution-route fees may overlap underlying venues; no component partition

venues.name: o1 Launchpad
venues.creatorEarningsDefinition: Actual swap credits allocated to creators and referrers, including amounts still unclaimed.

venues.name: clanker
venues.creatorEarningsDefinition: Token creator's LP rewards, claimable from the initial single-sided Uniswap v4 position.

venues.name: StonkBrokers
venues.creatorEarningsDefinition: Pad + sunrise reopen tax legs to the next-night boost pot (50%), the faction's own locked pool (10%), StockBooster (13.33%) and the game creator (13.34%), plus both legs of the flushed NFT royalties.

venues.name: Bags
venues.excludedReason: Solana DBC overlap; Robinhood and post-migration components not separated
venues.creatorEarningsDefinition: Creator fees paid to token creators, plus (on Robinhood Chain V2 and V3) the partner/referrer share carved out of the protocol share of trading fees.

venues.name: Rapid Launch
venues.creatorEarningsDefinition: 14% of collector fees, distributed to referral recipients.

venues.name: BaseStonk
venues.creatorEarningsDefinition: The creator's cut of the tax less what the treasury swept and what reached BSTONK holders: the creator's wallets, the launch token's own holders through its dividend distributor, the burn of the launch token and the hook-owned liquidity wedge, as each launch configured them.

venues.name: Foci
venues.creatorEarningsDefinition: Escrow credits to creators (their fee share and the creator tax) and to referrers, plus hook referral claims.

story.notice: Justin Drake (Ethereum Foundation researcher) posted on 2026-10-07 a call to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode" (migrating assets to addresses whose public keys stay hidden behind a hash); Vitalik Buterin posted the same day that he does not recommend scrambling to move funds today but that AI-accelerated math and quantum risks to cryptography deserve to be taken seriously; The Block reported Europol urging preparation for quantum threats. Business Insider quoted the call on 2026-10-08 and posts summarizing the debate were still appearing on 2026-10-12.

signalsInWeek.title: @drakefjustin: "Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for 'bunker mode'. My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash." (2026-10-07)
@VitalikButerin: "I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously" (2026-10-07)
@TheBlockCo: Europol is urging the crypto industry to begin preparing for quantum computing threats, warning that wallet keys are the primary point of exposure (2026-10-07)
